ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$. If $\angle AOB = 42^\circ$, $\angle DOE = 36^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle AOB=42^\circ$,\\
and $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$ and $\angle DOE=36^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOB=\angle BOC=42^\circ$,\\
$\angle COD=\angle DOE=36^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BOD=\angle BOC+\angle DOC=42^\circ+36^\circ=\boxed{78^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: All rays in the figure start from point O; within the shown region, looking counterclockwise starting from the right-side horizontal ray OA, they are in order OB, OC, OD, OE. That is to say, B is between A and C, D is between C and E, and ∠BOD is composed of the adjacent ∠BOC and ∠COD. Reasoning: Because OB is the angle bisector of ∠AOC, ∠AOB = ∠BOC. It is known that ∠AOB = 42°, therefore ∠BOC = 42°. Because OD is the angle bisector of ∠COE, ∠COD = ∠DOE. It is known that ∠DOE = 36°, therefore ∠COD = 36°. From the figure it can be seen that ∠BOD = ∠BOC + ∠COD = 42° + 36° = 78°.
